backlog.title: tmux-zoxide-sessions v1.0 — Greenfield MVP
backlog.description: Ship the complete plugin from the PRD verbatim spec: (1) the shared frecency resolver library (zoxide / rupa-z / auto), (2) the manual window-jump key binding, (3) the automatic session-created auto-relocate hook, plus full configuration (8 tmux options), README, and LICENSE. The plugin must pass the PRD §7 10-case verification matrix and satisfy §9 acceptance criteria on tmux 3.6b with real zoxide, a zoxide shim, and rupa/z. Architecture findings and two validated corrections live in plan/001_afc2c7373095/architecture/findings_and_risks.md — implementing agents MUST apply Correction A (rupa/z false-positive fix) and Correction B (resolve() exit-0 hardening).

subtasks.title: get_tmux_option() helper
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: get_tmux_option is the universal tmux-plugins idiom (see architecture/research_plugin_ecosystem.md §2 — found byte-identical in TPM, tmux-resurrect, tmux-continuum). `tmux show-option -gqv <name>` returns empty + exit 0 for an unset @-option, so the default-arg pattern is correct. resolve.sh is POSIX sh: use `_v=$(...)`, NOT the non-POSIX `local` keyword.
2. INPUT: scripts/lib/ directory exists (from P1.M1.T1.S1). PRD §5.3 gives the verbatim function.
3. LOGIC: Create scripts/lib/resolve.sh with `#!/bin/sh` shebang + the header comment from PRD §5.3, and define get_tmux_option() exactly as in PRD §5.3 (POSIX form: `_v=$(tmux show-option -gqv "$1" 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$_v" ] && echo "$_v" || echo "$2"`). This is the FIRST function in resolve.sh; subsequent subtasks (S2/S3/S4) append to this same file.
4. OUTPUT: scripts/lib/resolve.sh exists and is sourceable; get_tmux_option <name> <default> echoes the option value or the default. Consumed by S2/S3/S4 and by the run file (P1.M2.T2.S1).
5. MOCKING: Unit-test by placing a fake `tmux` earlier on PATH that prints canned `show-option -gqv` output; assert the default is returned when the option is unset/empty.
6. DOCS: none — internal helper, no user-facing/config surface.

subtasks.title: _resolve_zoxide() backend
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE (empirically verified, architecture/findings_and_risks.md): `zoxide query <q>` prints exactly one absolute path line on a match and EMPTY stdout + exit 0 on a no-match (no stderr noise). So callers must check output, not status. Gate on `command -v zoxide`; redirect stderr `2>/dev/null` as hygiene.
2. INPUT: resolve.sh with get_tmux_option() present (from P1.M1.T2.S1).
3. LOGIC: Append `_resolve_zoxide()` to scripts/lib/resolve.sh per PRD §5.3: `command -v zoxide >/dev/null 2>&1 && zoxide query -- "$1" 2>/dev/null`. (Use the `--` end-of-options guard from NOTE D in findings_and_risks.md — cheap hardening against a query that looks like a flag.) TDD: failing test for missing-binary (empty, no error) and match/no-match output, then implement.
4. OUTPUT: _resolve_zoxide <query> echoes zoxide's best match or empty; never errors if zoxide is absent. Consumed by P1.M1.T2.S4 (resolve dispatcher, auto/zoxide branches).
5. MOCKING: A fake `zoxide` shim on PATH returning a canned path (match), empty (no-match), or absent from PATH (missing-binary) — assert each.
6. DOCS: none — internal.

subtasks.title: _resolve_z() backend (rupa/z) — APPLY CORRECTION A
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE — 🔴 APPLY CORRECTION A (architecture/findings_and_risks.md §A; full corrected code is given there). The PRD §5.3 form `"$shell" -c '. "$1"; _z "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; pwd'` has a CONFIRMED BUG: rupa/z's `_z` silently `cd`s on a match but leaves cwd UNCHANGED on a no-match, so `pwd` returns the subshell's STARTING directory — a false-positive non-empty path. Empirically reproduced on this machine (no-match returned the plugin's own dir). This is dormant by default (@zoxide-sessions-z-sh unset) but breaks the `z` and `auto`-fallback paths when a user points at a real z.sh.
2. INPUT: resolve.sh with get_tmux_option() present (from P1.M1.T2.S1).
3. LOGIC: Append `_resolve_z()` using the VALIDATED before/after pwd-delta form from findings_and_risks.md §A (emit a path ONLY when `_z` actually changed cwd; source z.sh under zsh if available else sh; read @zoxide-sessions-z-sh; short-circuit `return 0` if unset/unreadable; always exit 0). TDD discipline: FIRST write a failing test that demonstrates the false positive (no-match query -> non-empty output), THEN implement the fix so no-match -> empty.
4. OUTPUT: _resolve_z <query> returns a path only on a real _z match, empty otherwise; always exit 0. Consumed by P1.M1.T2.S4 (resolve dispatcher, auto/z branches).
5. MOCKING: rupa/z is installed at /home/dustin/.config/znap/rupa/z/z.sh with a populated ~/.z — use it directly, or a temp HOME with a scratch ~/.z + a minimal z.sh fixture. Assert both a known match and a guaranteed no-match (empty output).
6. DOCS: none — internal. (The README 'Backends' section, authored in P1.M4.T1, already describes the resolver as returning empty on no-match — Correction A makes that statement TRUE.)

subtasks.title: resolve() dispatcher — APPLY CORRECTION B
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE — 🟡 APPLY CORRECTION B (architecture/findings_and_risks.md §B). The PRD §5.3 comment states resolve() 'Always exits 0 — callers must check the output, not the exit status,' but the code does not enforce it for the `zoxide`/`z` branches (the backend call is the last statement, so its status propagates). zoxide's no-match exit code varies by version. End resolve() with an unconditional `return 0` to honor the documented contract.
2. INPUT: resolve.sh now contains get_tmux_option(), _resolve_zoxide() (S2), _resolve_z() (S3).
3. LOGIC: Append resolve() per PRD §5.3: read @zoxide-sessions-backend (default `auto`); `case` over zoxide -> _resolve_zoxide, z -> _resolve_z, auto -> try zoxide then fall back to z (capture into `_r`, printf '%s\n' "$_r"). ADD a trailing `return 0` after the case (see findings_and_risks.md §B for exact code). TDD: assert exit status is 0 for every backend on both match and no-match.
4. OUTPUT: resolve <query> echoes the best-match directory or empty, and ALWAYS exits 0. This is the single resolver entry point consumed by P1.M2.T1.S1 (z-window.sh) and P1.M3.T1.S1 (z-session.sh).
5. MOCKING: Fake `tmux` (to set @zoxide-sessions-backend) + fake zoxide/z.sh fixtures; assert correct output and exit-0 for all three backends × {match, no-match}.
6. DOCS: none — internal.

milestones.title: Window-jump feature (manual)
milestones.description: Implement Feature A: prefix <key> opens a command-prompt; the typed query is resolved to a frecency directory and a new window opens there (named after the dir basename), falling back to the current pane's directory. This milestone delivers z-window.sh and creates the run file with the key binding.

tasks.title: scripts/z-window.sh handler
tasks.description: The run-shell target of the window-jump binding. Resolves the query via the shared backend and opens a new window in the resolved (or current) directory.

subtasks.title: Implement z-window.sh
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE (architecture/findings_and_risks.md §✅6): command-prompt `%%` substitution is textual and splits on spaces, BUT this script uses `query="$*"` which RECOMBINES the args, so spaced queries work correctly. Do not change to "$1".
2. INPUT: resolve() (always-exit-0, from P1.M1.T2.S4) via `. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/resolve.sh"`.
3. LOGIC: Create scripts/z-window.sh per PRD §5.4 verbatim. `#!/bin/sh`; `SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)`; source resolve.sh; `query="$*"`; read cur = `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_current_path}'` (fallback $HOME) and session = `... '#{session_name}'`; `dir="$cur"`; if query non-empty, `resolved=$(resolve "$query")` and use it if non-empty; `base=$(basename "$dir")`; `tmux new-window -t "$session:" -c "$dir" -n "$base"`. Make the file executable (chmod +x). TDD: empty query -> window in cur path; match -> window in resolved dir, named basename; no-match -> window in cur path.
4. OUTPUT: z-window.sh [query...] opens exactly one window in the resolved dir (named basename) or the current pane dir. Consumed by P1.M2.T2.S1 (the binding invokes it).
5. MOCKING: Drive an ISOLATED tmux server (`tmux -L zxstest ...`) so the user's live tmux is untouched; inject a fake `resolve`/zoxide for deterministic results; assert the new window's cwd via `tmux display-message -t <win> -p '#{pane_current_path}'` and name via '#{window_name}'.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] The @zoxide-sessions-key and @zoxide-sessions-prompt options this binding reads are documented in README.md's Options table, authored wholesale in P1.M4.T1 — no separate doc update in this subtask; just ensure the defaults ('g', 'z to:') match.

subtasks.title: Create run file with window binding
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE (architecture/research_plugin_ecosystem.md §1, external_deps.md §2): TPM executes `<plugin>.tmux` at the repo root ONCE per init/reload, output suppressed, so the run file must be `chmod +x` with a valid shebang and do its work via tmux commands (not stdout). Use `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `CURRENT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)` (TPM convention).
2. INPUT: get_tmux_option() from resolve.sh (P1.M1.T2.S1); the absolute path of z-window.sh (P1.M2.T1.S1).
3. LOGIC: Create tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux per PRD §5.2 PART 1 ONLY (do NOT add the session-hook block — that is P1.M3.T2.S1). Bash preamble, source resolve.sh, read key=get_tmux_option('@zoxide-sessions-key','g') and prompt=get_tmux_option('@zoxide-sessions-prompt','z to:'), then `tmux bind-key "$key" command-prompt -p "$prompt" "run-shell '$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-window.sh %%'"`. Make executable (chmod +x).
4. OUTPUT: tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux at repo root, executable, TPM-loadable, registering the window-jump binding. The file is APPENDED (not rewritten) by P1.M3.T2.S1 — keep the window-binding section intact and terminate it cleanly.
5. MOCKING: Load on an ISOLATED tmux server (`tmux -L zxstest`): source the run file's commands; assert `tmux list-keys | grep` shows `bind-key g`; trigger the prompt path with a query and confirm a window opens (this is also PRD §7 test #8).

milestones.title: Session auto-relocate feature (automatic)
milestones.description: Implement Feature B: a global session-created hook (backgrounded) that relocates the first pane of any new session that landed in $HOME to the zoxide-resolved dir matching its name. The $HOME guard makes it safe alongside resurrect/continuum/sessionx/sesh. This milestone delivers z-session.sh (the guard chain) and appends the hook wiring to the run file.

tasks.title: scripts/z-session.sh handler (guard chain)
tasks.description: The session-created handler. Implements the 11-step guard chain from PRD §3.2: master toggle, name, skip-list, locate first pane, read path, normalize+compare against home-dir, resolve, respawn-pane -c -k, optional rename.

subtasks.title: Implement z-session.sh guard chain
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE (architecture/findings_and_risks.md, external_deps.md §3): session-created fires AFTER the session+first pane exist, so display-message -t <name> -p '#{pane_id}' returns the new session's pane and '#{pane_current_path}' is readable (empirically confirmed). respawn-pane -c <dir> -k sets cwd, kills the old shell, and PRESERVES the window name + geometry (so an external rename-window hook is unaffected). The resurrect/continuum -c linchpin is confirmed from source, so the `path == $HOME` guard is a precise discriminator.
2. INPUT: get_tmux_option() and resolve() from resolve.sh (P1.M1.T2.S1, P1.M1.T2.S4). The session name arrives as a single $1 (the hook quotes "#{session_name}").
3. LOGIC: Create scripts/z-session.sh per PRD §5.5 verbatim — the full guard chain: (1) master toggle off -> exit; (2) name=$1 empty -> exit; (3) skip-names loop (default 'home main'); (4) pane=display-message -t "$name" -p '#{pane_id}'; (5) path=display-message -t "$pane" -p '#{pane_current_path}'; (6) home_dir option (default $HOME); (7) _norm() via readlink -f + trailing-slash collapse, compare path vs home -> exit if !=; (8) resolved=$(resolve "$name"); (9) respawn-pane -t "$pane" -c "$resolved" -k; (10) if @zoxide-sessions-window-name==session, rename first window to name. EVERY tmux call guarded `2>/dev/null || exit 0`. Make executable (chmod +x). TDD covers PRD §7 cases 1-4,6,7,9: relocate fires / skip-list / no-match / not-$HOME / master-off / window-name / spaced name.
4. OUTPUT: z-session.sh <name> relocates ONLY $HOME-landed, resolvable, non-whitelisted sessions; always exits 0. Consumed by P1.M3.T2.S1 (the hook invokes it).
5. MOCKING: ISOLATED tmux server (`tmux -L zxstest`). Create sessions whose first pane cwd is $HOME (expect relocate) vs /tmp (expect skip); set @zoxide-sessions-skip-names and auto-session=off; use a zoxide shim for deterministic resolve; assert pane cwd post-respawn via display-message -p '#{pane_current_path}'. For spaced-name handling (§7 test 9), temporarily prefix the script with an `echo "name=[$1]" >> /tmp/zxs.log` probe as the PRD suggests, then remove it.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] @zoxide-sessions-auto-session/-home-dir/-skip-names/-window-name are documented in README.md's Options table (P1.M4.T1) — ensure the defaults match.

tasks.title: session-created hook wiring (append to run file)
tasks.description: Append the session auto-relocate block to tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux: gate on @zoxide-sessions-auto-session and register the global session-created hook. Keep set-hook -g (reload-idempotent); document the composition tradeoff in README.

subtasks.title: Append session-created hook to run file
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE — 🟡 NOTE C (architecture/findings_and_risks.md §C): KEEP the PRD's `set-hook -g session-created` (empirically, `set-hook -g` OVERWRITES, which is RELOAD-IDEMPOTENT — the right choice for a plugin TPM re-sources on every reload; `set-hook -ag` would duplicate the hook each reload). The tradeoff: a global session-created hook set in .tmux.conf BEFORE the TPM init line is replaced. This contradicts the literal wording of PRD §6.2 — it is handled as a DOCS item in P1.M4.T1 / P1.M4.T3, NOT by changing the mechanism. Do not switch to -ag.
2. INPUT: tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux already exists with the window-binding section (from P1.M2.T2.S1); z-session.sh absolute path (from P1.M3.T1.S1).
3. LOGIC: APPEND the PRD §5.2 PART 2 block to tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux (preserve the window-binding section above): read auto_session=get_tmux_option('@zoxide-sessions-auto-session','on'); if [ "$auto_session" != 'off' ]; then SESSION_SCRIPT="$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-session.sh"; `tmux set-hook -g session-created "run-shell -b '${SESSION_SCRIPT} \"#{session_name}\"'"`; fi. Use the exact quoting from PRD §5.2 (single quotes around the run-shell arg, escaped double quotes around #{session_name}) so spaced names arrive as one $1.
4. OUTPUT: When loaded, the run file registers the session-created hook iff auto-session != off. Verify: `tmux show-hooks -g session-created` prints `run-shell -b "/<abs>/z-session.sh \"#{session_name}\""` (PRD §9 / §7 post-registration check).
5. MOCKING: ISOLATED tmux server (`tmux -L zxstest`): load the run file; assert the hook is registered when auto-session=on and ABSENT when =off; create a session at $HOME and confirm z-session.sh fires (probe log); create a session with a spaced name and confirm $1 is intact (§7 test 9).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] The hook-composition note (NOTE C) belongs in README.md's 'Scope & compatibility' section (P1.M4.T1) — flag it for that task.
